ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2020-09-15
Provider: Dr. Maria Rodriguez, MD
Department: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
3-month history of dull, aching pain in his left thigh and knee, progressively worsening after basketball.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 13-year-old male with asthma, atopic dermatitis, and obesity previously evaluated for pseudogynecomastia presents with left thigh and knee pain. The pain has progressively worsened, especially after physical activities such as playing basketball. He denies any recent trauma or injury.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Pseudogynecomastia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Asthma, mild persistent
- Atopic dermatitis (childhood eczema)
- Obesity (BMI >95th percentile for age)
- Sedentary lifestyle

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate inhalation aerosol 44 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled twice daily for asthma maintenance

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal obesity
- Paternal asthma
- Older brother with history of slipped capital femoral epiphysis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: 8th grade middle school student.

VITAL SIGNS:
His vital signs are within normal limits.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the patient walks with a slight limp favoring his left leg. There is no erythema or warmth over the knee or thigh, but he has limited internal rotation of the left hip.

IMAGING:
Radiographs of the left hip are obtained and demonstrate a posterior and medial displacement of the femoral head relative to the femoral neck.

Date: 2020-04-15
Provider: Dr. James Okafor, MD
Department: Pediatrics
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Lump beneath his left nipple noticed 3 weeks ago, unchanged in size.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 13-year-old male with mild persistent asthma, eczema, and obesity returns for evaluation of a left breast mass seen in Pediatric Endocrinology in January. He is brought to the clinic by his mother because of a lump beneath his left nipple that he noticed 3 weeks ago. The mass has not changed in size since it was first detected. The patient denies nipple discharge, skin changes, weight loss, or recent trauma to the chest.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Pseudogynecomastia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Asthma, mild persistent
- Atopic dermatitis (childhood eczema)
- Obesity (BMI >95th percentile for age)
- Sedentary lifestyle

He is otherwise healthy.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate inhalation aerosol 44 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled twice daily for asthma maintenance

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
There is no family history of breast or endocrine disease

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: 8th grade middle school student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On examination, his height and weight are appropriate for age. Secondary sexual characteristics are consistent with Tanner stage IV, including axillary hair and testicular enlargement. There is a 2.5-cm, mildly tender, rubbery, mobile mass directly under the left areola without overlying skin dimpling or erythema. No axillary lymphadenopathy is present, and the right breast is normal. The rest of the physical examination is unremarkable.

ENCOUNTER NOTE
Date: 2022-03-15
Provider: Dr. Michael Patel, MD
Department: Emergency Medicine
Visit Type: ed

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Persistent discomfort in his right thigh and groin that has worsened over the past 3 weeks after a soccer game, with progressive limp.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
The patient is a 15-year-old male with obesity, mild persistent asthma, and atopic dermatitis, previously evaluated in 2020 and 2021 for left hip, thigh, and knee pain, who presents with new-onset right thigh and groin discomfort. He first noticed a dull ache after participating in a weekend soccer game, which he attributed to overexertion. The pain has not resolved with rest or over-the-counter analgesics, and he has been avoiding physical activity at school. His mother has noticed a progressive limp, particularly when he climbs stairs. He also mentions feeling more tired than usual and says he sometimes feels stiffness in the mornings, although this usually improves within an hour. There is no history of trauma, recent travel, rashes, or fever.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Pseudogynecomastia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis of Left Hip (diagnosed 2021-11-15)
- Asthma, mild persistent
- Atopic dermatitis (childhood eczema)
- Obesity (BMI >95th percentile for age)
- Sedentary lifestyle

His past medical history includes childhood eczema and mild asthma treated with inhaled corticosteroids.

MEDICATIONS:
Home Medications:
- Albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate inhalation aerosol 44 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled twice daily for asthma maintenance

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal obesity
- Paternal asthma
- Older brother with history of slipped capital femoral epiphysis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
His diet is low in calcium-rich foods, and he spends most of his time indoors playing video games.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
His BMI is at the 97th percentile, and he is otherwise developmentally normal. On exam, he has a slightly externally rotated right lower extremity while standing. Gait assessment reveals limping and guarding on the right side. There is decreased range of motion at the right hip, especially with internal rotation. Knee and lumbar spine exams are unremarkable. There is no joint effusion or erythema. Neurologic exam is intact.

IMAGING:
A radiograph of the pelvis is shown below.

Provider: Dr. Maria Rodriguez, MD
Department: Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Visit Type: outpatient

CHIEF COMPLAINT:
3-month history of left hip pain radiating to the thigh and knee, worsening with activity and associated with a limp.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
This 14-year-old male with obesity and asthma returns to the orthopedic clinic with ongoing left lower extremity symptoms. He presents with a 3-month history of left hip pain that radiates to the thigh and occasionally to the knee. The pain worsens with activity and improves with rest. His mother reports that he has been walking with a limp.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
Active Problem List:
- Pseudogynecomastia (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Slipped capital femoral epiphysis (diagnosed 2020-09-15)
- Asthma, mild persistent
- Atopic dermatitis (childhood eczema)
- Obesity (BMI >95th percentile for age)
- Sedentary lifestyle

MEDICATIONS:
He takes albuterol inhaler as needed.

Home Medications:
- Albuterol sulfate inhalation aerosol 90 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled every 4-6 hours as needed for wheezing or shortness of breath
- Fluticasone propionate inhalation aerosol 44 mcg (2 puffs) inhaled twice daily for asthma maintenance

ALLERGIES:
NKDA

FAMILY HISTORY:
- Maternal obesity
- Paternal asthma
- Older brother with history of slipped capital femoral epiphysis

SOCIAL HISTORY:
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: None. Occupation: 8th grade middle school student.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION:
On physical examination, the patient has a waddling gait and limited internal rotation of the left hip. He is unable to bear weight on the left leg without experiencing pain.

LABORATORY DATA:
Complete blood count: within normal limits
- Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: 15 mm/hr (normal)
- C-reactive protein: 0.5 mg/dL (normal)

IMAGING:
An anteroposterior radiograph of the pelvis shows widening and irregularity of the left proximal femoral physis.
